en.title: Distinct Islands Under Translation Only
en.description:
1 represents land and 0 represents water; land cells connect up, down, left and right. Two island shapes are considered the same only if one can be translated to coincide with the other; rotations or reflections do not count as the same. Return the number of distinct shapes.

The standard input/output format was compiled by CSWork; value ranges marked "this site" are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: The first line contains r c, followed by r lines of 01 strings. On this site, 1≤r,c≤500.
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: there are 6 connected components, two pairs of which are translation-equivalent, giving 4 shapes in total. Example 2: the two vertical islands of length 2 coincide after translation, so the output is 1. Example 3: a horizontal two-cell island and a vertical two-cell island cannot coincide by translation alone, so the output is 2.
hints: Traverse each connected component, subtract the first visited coordinate from every coordinate in the component, sort them, and use the tuple as the shape signature.
